title: Conditions of Sale for Air Ticket Fare Brands: Travel Credit Vouchers
content:
These conditions govern a travel credit voucher raised against a ticket sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands.

**1. Value and expiry.**
1.1 A travel credit was formerly issued for the value the cancelled ticket still carried after any penalty had been withheld. That basis is no longer in force.
1.2 A voucher carries an expiry set by the travel credit validity term of the fare brand that produced it.

**2. The standing required before a voucher is raised.**
2.1 A voucher is issued only while the booking record stands at cancelled, refund pending or refunded.
2.2 That standing is taken from the company's own booking record and never from what the caller states the position to be, and it is read before the voucher is raised, not afterwards.
2.3 The record read is the one carried against the identifier of the very booking the voucher is to be raised against, so that the standing and the voucher belong to the same booking.

**3. The name on the voucher.**
3.1 The voucher is issued in the name of the traveller the ticket was issued to.
3.2 It is transferable only where the producing brand makes its credits transferable.

**4. Reissue after lapse.**
4.1 A lapsed voucher was formerly permitted to be reissued onto a fresh voucher against the reissue fee of the producing brand, the number of reissues permitted over the life of a voucher being 1. That basis is no longer in force.
4.2 A fresh voucher carries the same validity term as the voucher it replaces, counted from the day of reissue. Worked on a hypothetical reissue on 9 March 2027, under an illustrative validity term of 15 months used only to carry the counting through: the fresh voucher expires on 9 June 2028, standing on 9 June 2028 and lapsed on 10 June 2028.

**5. Brands that produce no voucher.** A brand whose travel credit validity term is zero issues no voucher at all, and the cancelled value is forfeited.

**6. No payment in money.** The value on a voucher is never paid out in money, not even where the traveller no longer intends to travel.
